blocks.sourceSectionTitle: What lifts a commerce graduate into the top band

rows: Excel to a high level, SQL, and one BI tool.
Plain-English reporting and one industry you know, such as retail or lending.
Accounting software, GST return work and reconciliation, done accurately.
Client communication and a monthly routine a shop owner can follow.
The exam subjects and training-year accuracy.
Spreadsheets, data fluency and the ability to explain numbers to a non-finance person.
Finding the right customer and starting the conversation.
A basic grip of numbers, such as margin, conversion and cost per lead.
A dashboard on a real or public dataset, with a one-page note on what a manager should do next.
Moving from reports people ask for to questions you raise, then to paid projects.
A sample GST calendar, a reconciliation checklist and a reference from one small business.
Moving from one-off filings to monthly packages for several clients.
Training-year work you can describe without breaching confidentiality, such as a process you improved.
Moving from a firm seat to a specialty, a senior industry role or your own practice.
A small campaign or outreach test with the replies and the result written down.
Moving from hitting a target to owning an account, a channel or a small team.

blocks.heading: AI By Route
blocks.sourceSectionTitle: AI by route: where it eats the entry job and where it adds pay

rows: Bookkeeping, data entry and clerical accounts

High. The World Economic Forum's Future of Jobs Report 2025 lists accounting, bookkeeping and payroll clerks, bank tellers and data entry clerks among the fastest-declining roles worldwide. Routine entry and matching are what software does first.
Now: use software to enter and match faster, and check every output. Later: move up to review, exceptions, advice and client handling, which stay with people.
Medium. First-pass checking and drafting get faster. Professional judgment, signing responsibility and client trust stay with a named person.
Now: draft notices and checklists with AI, then verify. Later: price on advice and review, not on hours of data entry.
Medium for routine reports. The same report lists big data specialists and FinTech engineers among the fastest-growing roles, so demand moves toward people who can frame the question.
Now: speed up cleaning and charting, and always verify. Later: choose the question and explain the answer to a client.
Medium. Drafting and list-building get faster. Trust, negotiation and knowing which customer to pursue stay human.
Now: use AI for research and first drafts. Later: run more tests per week and keep the human conversation.
Medium for counter work. Selection and the published scale do not depend on tools, but the daily work of tellers and clerks is the kind the report flags as shrinking.
Now: learn the digital banking tools in your role. Later: officer-level judgment and credit work carry the value.

figures.label: Median Monthly Entry Pay
figures.source: Commerce career options with salary run from about Rs 18,000 a month for a typical graduate in formal work to Rs 12 to 13 lakh a year for a placed, newly qualified CA, and the gap comes from the route you take, not from the commerce stream. The right early decisions, and a high-income skill portfolio built beside the degree, are what unlock the higher band and earlier financial freedom. This guide prices each route in rupees, years and risk.
